title: Kilo Code Operating Card
summary: Use Kilo Code modes, agent rules, approvals, and snapshots as a scoped workflow with independent Git and test verification.

sections.title: Choose a mode whose tools match the phase
paragraphs: Kilo Code provides planning, coding, debugging, orchestration, and custom agent modes across editor and CLI surfaces. Choose the least-capable mode that fits the current phase and review any requested mode expansion.
Custom modes can restrict commands and files. Snapshots or checkpoints support experimentation but do not replace repository Git history or release controls.

sections.title: Keep approval patterns narrow
paragraphs: Start interactively, inspect command and file approvals, and save only patterns that are safe for the current workspace. Avoid a blanket auto mode for unfamiliar repositories, tools, or network targets.
Version project agents and rules, review the complete Git diff, and run deterministic checks outside the model's narrative.

code.code:
Task: [one bounded outcome]
Scope: [workspace, paths, and mode]
Permissions: [files, shell patterns, network, tools, subagents]
Rules: [project agents and constraints]
Snapshot: [enabled recovery aid]
Verification: [Git diff and exact checks]
Recovery: [snapshot plus authoritative Git checkpoint]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the selected mode, permission decisions, rules, snapshot state, final Git diff, and test output. Confirm an automatic mode switch did not broaden file or tool access unexpectedly.
If the task crosses scope, stop approvals, preserve the trace, restore from a snapshot or Git checkpoint as appropriate, and retry in a narrower mode.

sections.title: First task: deterministic JSON inventory aggregation
paragraphs: Work in a version-controlled project directory named `kilo-inventory-lab`. Implement `aggregate_inventory(items)` in `inventory.py`. Each item must be a mapping with a non-empty string `sku` and an integer `quantity`. Boolean values are not valid integers for this contract, and negative quantities are invalid.

The function must sum duplicate SKUs, return a new list sorted by SKU, and never mutate the input list or any input mapping. Tests, Git metadata, unrelated files, secrets, external directories, and network access are outside the requested edit scope. Offline tests verify Python behavior only. They do not prove that a model call occurred or identify the selected model.

code.label: Task contract
code.code:
Input item: {"sku": string, "quantity": non-negative integer}
Output: [{"sku": string, "quantity": integer}, ...]
Rules:
1. Reject missing or malformed fields.
2. Reject bool quantities and negative quantities.
3. Sum duplicate SKUs.
4. Sort output by SKU ascending.
5. Do not mutate items or any item mapping.

sections.title: Create the lab without overwriting anything
paragraphs: From the new project directory, save the following as `setup_lab.py`, then run it with Python 3. The script preflights every destination before writing any destination. If any destination already exists, it refuses to write anything. It uses only the Python standard library and writes UTF-8 text with actual newline characters. No package installation is needed.

The JSON fixture is the input used by the human verification command. The CSV fixture is ancillary and is not read by `aggregate_inventory`; it is included only as a second-format inspection exercise.

sections.title: Configure Kilo CLI, Mistral, and scoped permissions
paragraphs: From the project directory, run `kilo --version`. For Kilo CLI 1.0+, run `kilo` separately to start the TUI. In the TUI, use `/connect` to configure an approved provider, `/models` to select an actually available model, `/agents` to switch agents, `/about` to inspect version and configuration paths, and `/diff` to compare changes. Record the exact version and model displayed by the learner's client. Those live values are UNKNOWN until observed. Source: https://kilo.ai/docs/code-with-ai/platforms/cli

Mistral is one supported provider, not the only valid choice. A Codestral key belongs with `codestral.mistral.ai`, while a La Plateforme key belongs with `api.mistral.ai`; do not interchange them. Enter a key only through the approved provider flow. Never place it in source, a project configuration file, the prompt, test output, or Git. Repository project environment references are ignored, so do not rely on them to supply a provider secret. The documentation does not guarantee any model's availability or pricing. Source: https://kilo.ai/docs/ai-providers/mistral and https://kilo.ai/docs/code-with-ai/platforms/cli

Project `kilo.jsonc` overrides the global configuration. Permissions use allow, ask, and deny, with the last matching pattern winning, so each broad rule appears before its exceptions. The read catchall requires reviewed approval for necessary lab reads, followed by explicit denials for root and nested sensitive names. The edit catchall denies every path, then allows only `inventory.py`, followed by the sensitive-name denials. A whole-value pattern such as `**/.env` contains a slash and therefore does not match root `.env`; root and nested forms are both listed. Wildcard matching is anchored to worktree-relative paths, normalizes backslashes, and uses the last matching rule. Source: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/blob/main/packages/opencode/src/util/wildcard.ts

These rules do not discover every possible secret, prove installed-runtime enforcement, or create an operating-system sandbox for processes or network activity. Keep auto-approve disabled, review every requested read, and stop on an unexpected path. `external_directory` does not restrict the underlying read or edit operations by itself, so it remains denied alongside shell, task, and network tools. Source: https://kilo.ai/docs/code-with-ai/platforms/cli

sections.title: Use a narrow custom primary agent
paragraphs: Create `.kilo/agents/inventory-lab.md` before launching the agent. Current custom agents support YAML frontmatter, `mode: primary`, and permission overrides. Configuration merges from global to project to directory definitions and then environment overrides. Last matching permission wins, so broad defaults must precede specific exceptions. Source: https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-modes

This agent may edit only `inventory.py`. Necessary nonsensitive lab reads require individual reviewed approval. Root and nested `.env` and `.env.local` files, `private.pem`, `secrets.txt`, and names containing `secret`, `credential`, or `token` are denied for both reading and editing. These name patterns are a boundary for this lab, not a claim that every secret can be identified by its filename.

The agent is primary, not a security sandbox. Natural-language instructions and configured permissions do not establish process or network isolation. Keep auto-approve disabled, retain the project policy, inspect actual changed paths, and have the human run all tests outside the agent.

code.label: .kilo/agents/inventory-lab.md

mode: primary
permission:

    "*": deny
    inventory.py: allow
    ".env": deny
    ".env.*": deny
    "**/.env": deny
    "**/.env.*": deny
    private.pem: deny
    "**/private.pem": deny
    secrets.txt: deny
    "**/secrets.txt": deny
    "*secret*": deny
    "**/*secret*": deny
    "*credential*": deny
    "**/*credential*": deny
    "*token*": deny
    "**/*token*": deny
  read:
    "*": ask
    ".env": deny
    ".env.*": deny
    "**/.env": deny
    "**/.env.*": deny
    private.pem: deny
    "**/private.pem": deny
    secrets.txt: deny
    "**/secrets.txt": deny
    "*secret*": deny
    "**/*secret*": deny
    "*credential*": deny
    "**/*credential*": deny
    "*token*": deny
    "**/*token*": deny
  bash: deny
  task: deny
  webfetch: deny
  websearch: deny
  external_directory: deny
---
You may edit only inventory.py.
Do not edit, run, or weaken tests.
Do not touch fixtures, configuration, Git metadata, secrets, or files outside this project.
Do not run commands, use the shell, access the web, inspect secrets, or call subagents.
Implement the stated aggregate_inventory contract.
Stop and report if the request crosses these boundaries.

sections.title: Launch Kilo and establish the baseline
paragraphs: Run the setup, version, and baseline commands from the directory containing `setup_lab.py`. Setup must precede the baseline. `kilo --version` reports the client version; it does not launch the interactive session. The Windows setup alternative is `py -3 setup_lab.py`, and the Windows baseline alternative is `py -3 -m unittest -v test_inventory.py`.

After setup, version capture, and the human-run baseline are complete, launch the interactive client separately by running `kilo`. Inside the TUI, use `/connect` to complete the approved provider flow, `/models` to select and record an actually available model, and `/agents` to select `inventory-lab`. Slash commands belong in the TUI, not in a shell command block. Source: https://kilo.ai/docs/code-with-ai/platforms/cli

The baseline contains four original tests and is expected to fail against the deliberately faulty implementation. This is an expected static result, not a claim that the commands were run for the learner. Actual version output, provider connection, model selection, approvals, and test output remain UNKNOWN until the learner records them.

python3 setup_lab.py
kilo --version
python3 -m unittest -v test_inventory.py

sections.title: Diagnose the concrete failure and recover narrowly
paragraphs: Python's default unittest loader sorts test method names, so this file runs `test_does_not_mutate_input` before `test_sums_duplicates_and_sorts`. Do not describe the sorting assertion as the first observed failure. Source: https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html

Each named test has a separate cause. `test_does_not_mutate_input` fails because `pop` removes `sku` and `quantity` from caller-owned mappings. `test_rejects_bool_and_negative_quantities` fails because the baseline accepts `True`, `False`, and `-1` instead of raising `ValueError`. `test_rejects_non_integer_quantity` fails because it accepts `1.5` instead of raising `ValueError`. `test_sums_duplicates_and_sorts` fails because the returned list follows first-seen dictionary insertion order, `b` then `a`, rather than the required sorted order, `a` then `b`. These are expected causes derived from the supplied code and tests, not fabricated live Kilo output.

The scoped repair is the existing corrected `inventory.py` reference: validate each record, read fields without mutation, aggregate duplicate SKUs, and construct the result in sorted SKU order. Do not edit or weaken either test file, fixtures, setup, configuration, Git metadata, secret-bearing paths, or anything outside the project. After the first task is independently verified, the separate reservations task changes the input and behavior while retaining the original function and all four original tests.

If an agent touches an out-of-scope path, stop it before approving more work. Inspect `git diff --stat`, `git diff --name-only`, and the complete diff. Do not use `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, or an unreviewed broad restore. Restore only each reviewed out-of-scope file from an authoritative Git checkpoint, or manually reverse that specific change. Then confirm that only `inventory.py` remains changed and retry the bounded prompt.

paragraphs: After reviewing the proposed source diff, the human must run the unit tests and then load the generated JSON fixture into `aggregate_inventory`. sections.title: Independent task: reservations and availability
paragraphs: Only after independently verifying the first task, create `test_inventory_reservations.py` with the complete tests below. This materially changes the requirement. Add `aggregate_available(inventory, reservations)` to `inventory.py` while preserving `aggregate_inventory` and `test_inventory.py`. Inventory quantities are stock. Reservation quantities reduce available stock. Duplicate SKUs in either input are summed. Every inventory SKU appears in sorted order. Reject malformed records, boolean or negative quantities, unknown reservation SKUs, and reservations greater than stock. Neither input may be mutated.
Run the new test file separately before looking at the answer key. Do not modify the original test file to make this task pass.

code.label: test_inventory_reservations.py complete independent test
code.code:
import copy
import unittest

from inventory import aggregate_available


class ReservationTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_sums_and_computes_available_without_mutation(self):
        inventory = [
            {"sku": "b", "quantity": 5},
            {"sku": "a", "quantity": 8},
            {"sku": "a", "quantity": 2},
        ]
        reservations = [
            {"sku": "b", "quantity": 2},
            {"sku": "a", "quantity": 4},
            {"sku": "a", "quantity": 1},
        ]
        inventory_before = copy.deepcopy(inventory)
        reservations_before = copy.deepcopy(reservations)
        self.assertEqual(
            aggregate_available(inventory, reservations),
            [
                {"sku": "a", "available": 5},
                {"sku": "b", "available": 3},
            ],
        )
        self.assertEqual(inventory, inventory_before)
        self.assertEqual(reservations, reservations_before)

    def test_zero_reservation_is_available(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            aggregate_available([{"sku": "x", "quantity": 2}], []),
            [{"sku": "x", "available": 2}],
        )

    def test_rejects_unknown_or_excess_reservation(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            aggregate_available(
                [{"sku": "x", "quantity": 2}],
                [{"sku": "y", "quantity": 1}],
            )
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            aggregate_available(
                [{"sku": "x", "quantity": 2}],
                [{"sku": "x", "quantity": 3}],
            )

    def test_rejects_bool_and_negative_quantities(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            aggregate_available([{"sku": "x", "quantity": True}], [])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            aggregate_available(
                [{"sku": "x", "quantity": 2}],
                [{"sku": "x", "quantity": -1}],
            )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

sections.title: Run both suites and provide causal feedback
paragraphs: For the corrected first task, the expected result is `4 tests ... OK`, with all four original tests unchanged and the reviewed source diff limited to `inventory.py`. The setup script now writes `sample_inventory.json` using `json.dumps(..., indent=2)` followed by an actual newline, so the fixture is valid JSON. The expected fixture result is `[{'sku': 'a', 'quantity': 5}, {'sku': 'b', 'quantity': 2}]`. These are expected results from the supplied implementation and fixture, not claims of a live run.

For the independent changed-input task, append the supplied `aggregate_available` answer without replacing `aggregate_inventory`, retain both test files unchanged, and run `python3 -m unittest -v test_inventory.py test_inventory_reservations.py`. The expected result is `8 tests ... OK`: four original tests plus four independent reservation tests. Inspect the diff and run both suites again. Actual learner output remains UNKNOWN until recorded.

Causal feedback for the first task is specific: avoiding `pop` preserves caller-owned mappings; explicit checks reject booleans, negative values, and non-integer quantities; accumulation combines duplicate SKUs; and sorting the keys produces deterministic SKU order. Causal feedback for the independent task is also separate: independently aggregating stock and reservations handles duplicates, validation rejects malformed quantities and unknown or excessive reservations, and subtraction computes availability without mutating either changed input.

Snapshots are enabled by default and stored in separate Git data outside the project, leaving the project's real Git history unchanged. A UI revert corresponds to a user-message checkpoint, not an arbitrary file or execution step. If snapshots are disabled or unavailable, only the conversation may rewind. Ignored files are excluded, and unsaved, manual, or external changes are not guaranteed to be protected. Stop the agent, inspect actual paths, and use authoritative project Git for reviewed recovery. Do not claim that a snapshot reverses network, remote, or other external effects. Source: https://kilo.ai/docs/code-with-ai/features/checkpoints

sections.title: Official workflow boundaries and unknown live facts
paragraphs: Kilo CLI documentation states that CLI 1.0+ uses `kilo --version`, starts a TUI, and provides `/connect`, `/models`, `/agents`, `/about`, and `/diff`. It also states that project `kilo.jsonc` overrides the global configuration and that permission matching uses allow, ask, and deny with the last matching pattern winning. Source: https://kilo.ai/docs/code-with-ai/platforms/cli

Kilo's Mistral documentation distinguishes the Codestral endpoint `codestral.mistral.ai` from the La Plateforme endpoint `api.mistral.ai` and instructs users to select an actually available model. It does not establish an exact model ID or guarantee availability or pricing. Source: https://kilo.ai/docs/ai-providers/mistral
Current custom-agent documentation supports `.kilo/agents/name.md` with YAML frontmatter, including `mode: primary` and permission overrides. Source: https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-modes

The following facts remain UNKNOWN unless observed and recorded from the actual learner client: exact Kilo version, provider approval, exact Mistral model identity, actual permission decisions, actual enforcement behavior, agent response, changed paths, and test execution results. Offline tests do not establish that a model call occurred. No fabricated UI, model identity, live outcome, or hidden answer-reveal control is claimed.
